usage.desc: Six chart families in one component, with no native dependency. React Native has no vector canvas across Expo SDK 54–58, so everything here is composed out of View: bars, a rotated rectangle per line segment, and a clipped half-disc per slice.

bar, line, area, pie, donut and radar. The prop is a discriminated union, so innerRadius on a bar chart does not compile. bar adds orientation and stacked; line and area add smooth, dots and decimate; pie and donut differ only in innerRadius; radar measures from the centre, so its minimum is always zero.
Rows in, one column per series. In a pie the categories are the rows rather than the columns, so only the first series is read — and the legend lists the rows instead.
The cheapest filter a chart has. 'toggle' (the default with two or more series) turns a series off on tap; it repeats the series colour, so it never has to explain what it turns off.
Renders your controls above the chart and reports the change. Chart does not filter anything — what "last 7 days" means belongs to whoever has the data.

A tap selects a whole category: the tooltip shows every visible series and everything else dims. The touch target is the band, not the mark — tapping a 2px line is impossible. Tapping the same point again lets it go.
Pair it with window whenever the data moves. Without it the selection is held by index, and in a sliding window the index shifts: the highlight silently ends up on a different datum.

The three that make a live chart readable. domain='sticky' stops the axis rearranging on every tick; window keeps the last N rows; decimate thins a line with LTTB down to what the measured width can show. Bars are never thinned — a missing bar reads as missing data.

Derived from the theme, not listed: the first series reuse its accents and the rest rotate the primary's hue. Every one clears 3:1 against surface, the WCAG minimum for a graphical object. Override one series at a time with series[].color.
Required: a chart has no text of its own to describe it. Each band also carries its category and its numbers, so a screen reader can walk the data.

data.description: The rows. Each one is a category on the x axis plus a number per series.

series.description: The series to draw. In 'pie'/'donut' only the first is used: the categories of a pie are its rows, not its columns.

xKey.description: The column holding each row's label.

selectBy.description: Stable identity for a row. Without it the selection is held by index, and in a sliding window the index moves: the highlight ends up pointing at another datum with nobody touching it. With it the highlight follows its datum, and disappears only once the datum leaves the window.

window.description: Draws only the last N rows — the sliding window of a live chart, so whoever pushes the data does not have to trim it on every tick.

height.description: Height of the drawing area, not counting filters or legend.

legend.description: 'toggle' turns the legend into the cheapest filter a chart has: tapping a series turns it off.
legend.default: 'auto' — toggle with two or more series, none with one

hiddenKeys.description: Series that are off, controlled. Without it Chart remembers them on its own.

onHiddenKeysChange.description: Reports the new set of hidden series.

filters.description: Controls above the chart, one per filter. Chart shows them and reports the change; it does not filter anything itself.

selected.description: The highlighted point, controlled. null means none.

onSelect.description: Reports the point that was tapped, or null when the selection is released.

tooltip.description: Balloon with the values of the category that was tapped.

formatValue.description: Formats every number on the axis and in the tooltip.

animate.description: Bars travel to their new value instead of jumping. Turn it off for high-frequency updates.

duration.description: Milliseconds the marks take to animate.

emptyText.description: Shown when there is nothing left to draw.

accessibilityLabel.description: Required: a chart has no text of its own to describe it.

type.description: The family of mark to draw. A discriminated union: the props of one type do not typecheck on another.

orientation.description: 'horizontal' puts the categories on the vertical axis.

stacked.description: Stacks the series instead of placing them side by side.

barRadius.description: Radius of the free end of each bar.

domain.description: Fixes the value axis. By default it is recomputed with every datum, which is right for a static chart and worst for a live one: a higher value arrives, the whole scale rearranges and the line jumps although the datum did not move. [min, max] is exact, with no rounding; 'sticky' starts from the data and grows when something does not fit, but never gives the room back.

grid.description: Reference lines on the value axis.

ticks.description: Ticks wanted on the value axis; rounding may give one more or one less.

decimate.description: How many points to draw at most, chosen with LTTB. false draws them all.
decimate.default: the measured width — one point per two pixels

smooth.description: Catmull-Rom instead of straight segments. The curve passes through every original point.

fillOpacity.description: Opacity of the fill under the line.

innerRadius.description: Hole as a fraction of the radius, 0–0.9.

sliceLabels.description: What to write on each slice. A slice narrower than 18° gets none — the label would land on its neighbours.

fill.description: Fills the polygon as well as drawing its outline.
